issues.title: Incorrect last augmented entropy variable
issues.failure_explanation: The augmented entropy variables must be the gradient of the energy with respect to (h,hu_m,hα,b). Equation eq:Total:Energy contains the term ghb, so its derivative with respect to the added coordinate b is gh. The old final component b is equal to that derivative only under an unstated accidental relation b=gh and therefore fails the construction's entropy-gradient contract.
issues.overall_effect: The published augmented vector is not the entropy gradient, so any identity treating all of its components as entropy variables is misstated. The bottom flux row and bottom dissipation block are zero, so the listed formal EC-flux and well-balanced conclusions do not genuinely depend on the erroneous last entry.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last component of the augmented entropy-variable vector by gh, so that it is the gradient of the augmented energy with respect to b. In uses of the dissipation or well-balanced argument, note that the zero bottom block annihilates the last entropy-variable jump; no flux or formal conclusion needs to change.
issues.why_classification: The term ghb in the old energy and the stated gradient definition uniquely force ∂E/∂b=gh. The entry b is a one-component transcription error, and its literal value is not used by the EC, ES, or well-balanced conclusions because the corresponding bottom rows and dissipation block are zero.

issues.title: Sign-dependent entropy-conservative fluctuation construction
issues.failure_explanation: The preceding definition requires D^- to use the left state with fEC-f(u^-), while D^+ must use the right state with f(u^+)-fEC. The old EC construction assigns the former expression to both. For example, take zero velocities and moments, constant b=0, h^-=1, and h^+=2. Both physical and EC fluxes vanish, so the old momentum fluctuations are g/2 and g/2, whose sum is g. The linear-path integral required by eq:path_conservation_cond is ∫_0^1 g(1+s) ds=3g/2. Thus the published pair fails its path-conservation contract.
issues.overall_effect: For general interfaces, the EC and ES DG constructions use a fluctuation pair that is not the declared trapezoidal path-conservative pair, so their general interface consistency and entropy-conservative construction are not justified by the old formula. The lake-at-rest lemma is not dependent because both old branches still vanish on that restricted state.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the EC fluctuation formula by D_EC^±(u−,u+)=½B(u±)(u+−u−) ± (f(u±)−f^EC(u−,u+)). Equivalently, retain the published expression for D_EC^− and use D_EC^+=½B(u+)(u+−u−)+f(u+)−f^EC for the plus branch. Use this pair throughout the EC and ES schemes.
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding general fluctuation definition uniquely determines the state and sign in each branch; the old right-hand side is simply the minus branch copied under a ± label. Substitution restores the declared trapezoidal path-conservation identity without changing the EC flux, proof architecture, or lake-at-rest behavior.

issues.title: Nonzero SWE residual in the entropy decomposition
issues.failure_explanation: For N=1, take h^-=h^+=1, u_m^-=u_m^+=1, equal bottoms, α_1^-=0, and α_1^+=1. Then eq:SWME:Entropy:Variables gives jump(w1)=-1/6, the first component of the displayed SWE EC flux is avg(hu_m)=1, and the B^SWE term vanishes because the height and bottom jumps are zero. Hence the left side of the old equation is -1/6, not zero; it equals the residual shown in version 2. The old proof of thm:ec_flux drops this SWE residual while also omitting its cancelling counterpart from the linearized-moment block.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone SWE block identity is false, and the old hierarchical proof of thm:ec_flux is invalid as written. The numerical flux itself can remain unchanged because the omitted SWE residual cancels a term in the combined SWLME contribution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the zero on the right of the SWE block identity by −½Σ_j jump(α_j²)avg(hu_m)/(2j+1). In the proof of thm:ec_flux, retain the linearized-moment term Σ_j jump(α_j)avg(hu_m)avg(α_j)/(2j+1); it cancels that residual because jump(α_j²)=2avg(α_j)jump(α_j). Group the SWE and linearized-moment blocks before obtaining jump(u_mΨ), leaving the numerical flux and the full-moment block unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine omitted-term error in an intermediate identity and therefore not a typo. Nevertheless, the old formulas already contain the cancelling term, and a short local algebraic regrouping restores the unchanged entropy-conservative flux and thm:ec_flux without a new lemma, new construction, or meaningful loss of guarantee.

issues.title: Malformed averaged inverse entropy-Hessian matrix
issues.failure_explanation: At u_m=0 and α=0 with h>0, eq:Total:Energy has Hessian diag(g,1/h,1/(3h),...), so its inverse begins with 1/g. The old construction has y_1=1 and z_1=1, producing (1+1)/g=2/g. For constant bottom and a pure height jump it therefore maps jump(w1)=g jump(h) to 2 jump(h), contradicting the asserted jump map. Moreover, the last diagonal coefficient (2n+1)gh depends on the Manning parameter rather than the number N of moments.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed dissipation matrix is not the claimed inverse entropy Hessian and does not provide the asserted state-to-entropy jump conversion. Its extra positive leading entry can still leave the quadratic dissipation nonnegative, so the old well-balanced lemma is not defeated solely by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace z by (0,gh,3gh,…,(2N+1)gh)^T in the definition of the averaged matrix. A direct local calculation from the stated energy then gives H̄=g^−1(avg(y)avg(y)^T+diag(avg(z))), establishes the unaugmented state-to-entropy jump map for constant bottom, and shows positive definiteness for h>0. Retain the zero block in the augmented bathymetry coordinate.
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and preserves the ES and well-balanced constructions, but the leading 1 is not merely an evident notation slip: detecting that it must be 0 requires checking the entropy Hessian or its inverse. That routine local calculation, together with replacing the moment-independent n by N, resolves the defect without nontrivial new architecture or any loss of guarantee, so the issue is minor rather than moderate.

issues.title: Unscaled tensor identity in the computational construction
issues.failure_explanation: Because tilde(A_ijk)=A_ijk/(2i+1) and tilde(B_ijk)=B_ijk/(2i+1), eq:condition implies A_kji=-((2k+1)/(2i+1))B_ijk-B_kji, not the old unscaled formula. For i=j=1 and k=2, the supplied Legendre definitions give B_112=1/5, B_211=-1, and A_211=2/3; the old instruction instead returns 4/5. Thus an implementation following the appendix computes a tensor inconsistent with eq:Aijk_Bijk.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's executable tensor construction can generate the wrong A tensor and hence a different numerical moment flux. The analytic energy and EC-flux results use the integral definitions themselves and therefore are not dependent on this erroneous implementation shortcut.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the computational identity with scaled tensors as Ã_kji=−(B̃_ijk+B̃_kji). If an implementation stores the unscaled tensors, use the equivalent formula A_kji=−((2k+1)/(2i+1))B_ijk−B_kji.
issues.why_classification: Equation eq:condition and the definitions of the scaled coefficients directly and uniquely force the tilded identity; the appendix merely dropped the tildes when transcribing that relation. Correcting the notation or expanding the already-defined scaling requires no new mathematical argument and does not affect results based on the integral tensor definitions.
